speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Desired by all — yet whose change?
premises: From change, that One is desired for all spirits (pariṇāmāt tad ekaṃ hi sarvān puṃsaḥ pratīṣyate).
Yet body-earth-and-rest's change is by nature (tathāpi dehabhūtādeḥ pariṇāmaḥ svabhāvataḥ).
inference: The grant (all desire the One) pressed by the body-case.
uncertainties: taye pāṭhāntara for tathāpi in apparatus — sense stable under either; print reading kept.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Why not for the deemed-freed?
premises: As before — why would it not be, toward the deemed-freed (pūrvavan na bhavet kasmāt taṃ muktābhimataṃ prati)?
Yet it does occur — but is not joined by him (athāpi sa bhavaty eva kiṃ tu tena na yujyate).
inference: Occurrence without union — the freed-spirit test.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Needlessness — whose?
premises: By the freed spirit — done with tasks, need-free — he stands alone (mukta-puṃsā kṛtārthatvād anarthitvāt sa kevalaḥ).
Not so: needlessness belongs to no spirit ever, nor to mind (naitan nārthitvam asyāsti jātu puṃso'tha cetasaḥ).
inference: The objector's need-free spirit denied on both sides.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: No reunion — and yet born?
premises: With need gone, no meeting with spirit again would be (arthitvavigamān na syād bhūyaḥ puṃsā samāgamaḥ).
This too is unjust, once body-dwelling mind is born (tad etad api na nyāyyaṃ jāte dehasthacetasi).

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Mokṣa — nature or karma's end?
premises: If from perceptible-only-nature of that, not from karma's waning (saṃvedyaikasvabhāvatvāt tasya karmakṣayān na cet).
Mokṣa would be mere nature, resting on karma's waning (tat svabhāvatvam eva syān mokṣaḥ karmakṣayāśrayaḥ).
inference: The view collapses mokṣa into nature.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Mercy-acts — passionless?
premises: There'd be acts even of spirit-distinction-knowers, from compassion (syur jñātapuṃvivekānāṃ karmāṇy api kṛpāditaḥ).
If not from passion — thus mokṣa from passion's exhaustion (na rāgāt tāni ced evaṃ mokṣo rāgakṣayād bhavet).
inference: Compassion smuggles passion back; the view becomes passion-exhaustion doctrine.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Abandoned — what stands?
premises: Thus view-abandoned — that nature-view is unjust (tathā ca darśanatyāgas tan na yuktā svabhāvadṛk).
Hence body-and-rest, famously, have sentient-maker as prior (tasmāt prasiddhaṃ tanvādi buddhimatkartṛpūrvakam).
inference: The siddhānta: bodies bespeak a knowing maker.
uncertainties: svabhāvadṛk agrees with yuktā (the abandoning is nature-viewed).

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Proved — by what?
premises: This flawless proof (ity etan niravadyaṃ prasādhanam).

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Aimed at whom — shaken by what?
premises: This reason, aimed at the Supreme Lord by the self-entrusted self (sa eṣa hetuḥ parameśvaraṃ prati prayujyamānaḥ svaniveśitātmanā).
Not overpowered by reason-faults in the least (na hetudoṣaiḥ paribhūyate manāk).
Nor the rival's either — only this is said (paro'pi vā kevalam etad ucyate).
inference: The hetu stands aimed at the Lord; rivals answered, disputation closed.
uncertainties: kevalam-etad-ucyate scope: 'only this is said' closes the disputation.
